headline: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey calls for India to 'reclaim' Noakhali, Ctg Port, Sylhet from Bangladesh
summary: Dubey claims these territories were forcibly handed to East Pakistan during Partition without the consent of the erstwhile Tripura kingdom's ruler, blaming India's first prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
details: BJP lawmaker Nishikant Dubey has publicly called for India to "reclaim" three significant Bangladeshi territories: Noakhali, Chittagong Port, and Sylhet. He made these controversial remarks on Friday, according to The Hindu.

Dubey alleged that these regions were handed over to East Pakistan during the 1947 Partition without the consent of the ruler of the erstwhile Tripura kingdom. He specifically blamed India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, for this decision.

According to The Hindu, Dubey claimed Nehru agreed to exclude these regions from India to secure the Muslim League's support in the 1946 interim government. He stated, "The time has come not just to reclaim Pakistan-occupied Kashmir... It is also time to reclaim the territories that Nehru ji forcibly handed over."

His remarks received support from Pradyot Manikya, a descendant of Tripura’s royal family and head of the Tipra Motha party. Manikya stated that large parts of the erstwhile Tripura Kingdom were seceded to East Pakistan without his grandmother's knowledge.

Manikya further linked the loss of Chattogram (Chittagong) to the northeastern Indian region's current lack of direct sea access. He argued that this decision left the region geographically constrained, impacting its connectivity.

Dubey also quoted Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya, the then king of Tripura, who allegedly opposed the interim government's decision. The king reportedly challenged Nehru, asserting that the territories were his kingdom and he should decide their fate.

headline: Dhaka South City Corporation offers 18 job opportunities in 9th & 10th grade
summary: A total of 18 positions are open in the revenue sector, with the application deadline set for November 26, 2026. Interested candidates can apply online through the official website.
details: Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has published a job circular for 18 positions in its revenue sector. These opportunities are for the 9th and 10th grade levels.
The application process begins on November 5, 2026, at 10 AM, and the deadline for submission is November 26, 2026, at 5 PM.

The application fee is BDT 223 for general candidates. A reduced fee of BDT 56 applies to underprivileged groups, including minority ethnic communities, physically challenged individuals, and third-gender applicants.
